title: Modi flies to Manila as South China Sea code misses deadline and a Quad meeting takes shape
dek: The Prime Minister attends the ASEAN-India and East Asia summits on Tuesday. China's premier told ASEAN to resist 'outside interference' as the region's talks with Beijing on a maritime code ran out of time again.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi left for Manila on Monday for the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, both on Tuesday, 17 November, arriving in a region where talks between China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations on a South China Sea code of conduct have missed another deadline and where US President Donald Trump is expected to join a meeting of Quad leaders.

In his departure statement, Mr Modi said India's relationship with ASEAN countries was "at the heart of India's Act East Policy" and that he expected the visit to "impart new energy" to the partnership and to a "peaceful, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific". He is travelling at the invitation of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., whose country chairs ASEAN this year, and will attend a dinner Mr Marcos is hosting for visiting leaders on Monday evening.

## What happened

Mr Modi's statement said ties "rooted in centuries of civilisational exchanges" had grown into a partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-to-people links, and that he looked forward to exchanging views with other leaders "on strengthening peace, stability and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific". He said he would also meet members of the Indian community in the Philippines. The visit runs from 16 to 18 November, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) has said, with bilateral meetings with other leaders in between the summits.

The Manila meetings opened under the shadow of US-China rivalry. Speaking at the ASEAN summit on Monday, Chinese Premier Li Qiang, who represents President Xi Jinping, praised China's ties with the bloc. "The past five years have been truly extraordinary, and the achievements we scored have not come easily," he said, according to reports. He said China remained "firmly committed to safeguarding multilateralism and promoting free trade", and that it was more important than ever for China and ASEAN to stand united and resist outside interference. China's annual trade with ASEAN passed $1 trillion last year, reports said.

The code of conduct that ASEAN and China have been negotiating for more than two decades will not be finished this year. The Philippines' foreign secretary, Maria Theresa Lazaro, said on Saturday that "80 percent of the document itself is finished" but that some important points were unresolved, according to reports. In 2023 the two sides had agreed to conclude it within three years. The hardest unresolved issue is the code's geographic scope: Beijing claims almost the entire sea, a claim an international arbitral tribunal rejected in 2016 in a case brought by the Philippines. China does not accept that ruling.

Trump is due in Manila on Tuesday, at the end of the summits, and is expected to meet ASEAN leaders before flying to the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, where a three-way meeting with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin is planned, according to reports. Several reports say the leaders of the Quad (India, the United States, Japan and Australia) are scheduled to meet in Manila on Tuesday evening, after Trump arrives. Japan has confirmed Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's participation in the Manila meetings, one report said, but the MEA had not confirmed a Quad meeting when it briefed reporters last week, and no joint announcement from the four governments had been published by Monday afternoon.

## Background

The East Asia Summit brings ASEAN's members together with eight other countries, including India, China, the United States, Russia and Japan, and is the region's main leaders' forum on security. 2026 is the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation, and next year marks 35 years of dialogue relations and five years of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

The Philippines has been at the centre of the sea dispute with China. China's coast guard has repeatedly used water cannon against Philippine vessels near disputed features such as Second Thomas Shoal, and clashes have caused collisions and injuries. In the days before the summit, China's foreign minister Wang Yi urged Manila to rein in its politicians and "speak with one voice" on China policy, reports said. China's ambassador to the Philippines, Jing Quan, said China "may easily win" if it used force but "will not choose force", according to reports.

India has stepped up defence ties with Manila. The Philippines bought three shore-based batteries of the India-Russia BrahMos cruise missile in 2022 for $375 million, and India is in talks to supply more, according to reports.

## India's stake and the risks

India has no claims in the South China Sea but a large stake in it: much of its trade with East Asia, including electronics and components from China, moves through it. At last week's briefing, Rudrendra Tandon, the MEA's Secretary (East), said any code of conduct must conform to international maritime law, specifically the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), and must respect the legitimate rights of countries that are not party to the negotiations. That concern is practical: a code drafted only between China and ASEAN could, if its scope or terms favoured Beijing, restrict how navies and companies from outside the region operate there, including Indian oil and gas interests off Vietnam.

Trade is the other pressure point. India's trade with ASEAN is about $122 billion a year, and New Delhi imports far more from the bloc than it sells, a gap it blames partly on the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement in force since 2010. India wants the agreement's review finished quickly; Mr Tandon said reaching consensus among ASEAN's members and India was complex and time-consuming. A slow review leaves Indian manufacturers competing with goods from ASEAN countries, some of which use Chinese inputs, at low tariffs.

On Myanmar, which borders four north-eastern states and through which the India-funded Kaladan transport project links Kolkata port to Sittwe, Mr Tandon said isolating the country's military government was "not the right approach" because it could open space for other external players.

## What they are saying

Beijing presents the region's future as one of economic integration free from outside interference, a phrase it commonly uses to criticise US alliances. Manila's foreign ministry spokesman, Dominic Xavier Imperial, said the Philippines wanted the code to respect the rights of countries outside the region, reports said, a position close to India's. Analysts in Manila told reporters that trade and supply-chain worries were likely to dominate the summit agenda more than the sea dispute.

## What happens next

- Monday, 16 November: dinner hosted by President Marcos for visiting leaders
- Tuesday, 17 November: ASEAN-India Summit and East Asia Summit; Trump arrives; a Quad leaders' meeting is expected in the evening, according to reports
- Later this week: APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen, with a planned Trump-Xi-Putin meeting
- Mid-December: G20 summit in the United States, where Mr Modi and Mr Trump are also expected, according to reports
